geelong-1.name: Geelong Waterfront
geelong-1.bio: Corio Bay shoreline redeveloped from the old port, with 100-plus painted bollards and a c.1892 steam carousel.

geelong-2.name: National Wool Museum
geelong-2.bio: Museum of wool, fibre and textiles in the former Dennys, Lascelles woolstore, opened in 1988.

geelong-3.name: You Yangs Regional Park
geelong-3.bio: Granite peaks rising from the plains, with Flinders Peak views to Melbourne and Geelong and over 50 km of trails.

geelong-4.name: Geelong Botanic Gardens
geelong-4.bio: Botanic garden in Eastern Park, established in 1850 and the fourth oldest in Australia.

bellarine-peninsula-1.name: Queenscliff
bellarine-peninsula-1.bio: Town at the Bellarine Peninsula's tip, home to Fort Queenscliff and the terminus of the Bellarine Railway.

bellarine-peninsula-2.name: Fort Queenscliff
bellarine-peninsula-2.bio: 1860 fort guarding the entrance to Port Phillip, entered by weekend guided tour only; bring ID.

bellarine-peninsula-3.name: Bellarine Peninsula Railway
bellarine-peninsula-3.bio: Volunteer-run steam railway from Queenscliff along 16 km of former branch line towards Drysdale.

bellarine-peninsula-4.name: Barwon Heads
bellarine-peninsula-4.bio: Seaside town at the Barwon River mouth with river swimming, bridge walks and views from The Bluff over Bass Strait.

bellarine-peninsula-5.name: Point Lonsdale
bellarine-peninsula-5.bio: Headland with a 1902 lighthouse overlooking The Rip, the entrance to Port Phillip, viewed from outside.

surf-coast-1.name: Bells Beach
surf-coast-1.bio: Surf beach near Torquay that has hosted the Rip Curl Pro, the world's longest-running pro surf contest, since 1962.

surf-coast-2.name: Australian National Surfing Museum
surf-coast-2.bio: Torquay museum with the Australian Surfing Hall of Fame and boards from early wooden designs to modern ones.

surf-coast-3.name: Split Point Lighthouse
surf-coast-3.bio: Aireys Inlet lighthouse, the 'White Lady' of Round the Twist, with a climb to the top for 360-degree coastal views.

surf-coast-4.name: Torquay
surf-coast-4.bio: Bass Strait town 21 km south of Geelong, gateway to the Great Ocean Road and home of the national surfing museum.

surf-coast-5.name: Anglesea
surf-coast-5.bio: Great Ocean Road town at a tidal river mouth, where eastern grey kangaroos live on the golf course.

surf-coast-6.name: Point Addis
surf-coast-6.bio: Great Ocean Road stop near Bells Beach, with a short boardwalk to a lookout over sandstone cliffs and beaches.

surf-coast-7.name: Torquay Surf Beach
surf-coast-7.bio: Main surf beach of Torquay, home of Australian surfing and gateway to the Great Ocean Road, near Bells Beach.

surf-coast-8.name: Great Ocean Road Memorial Arch
surf-coast-8.bio: Timber-log arch over the Great Ocean Road at Eastern View, honouring the returned servicemen who built the road.

lorne-1.name: Teddy's Lookout
lorne-1.bio: Viewing platform in Queens Park above Lorne, looking over the St George River estuary and the Great Ocean Road.

lorne-2.name: Erskine Falls
lorne-2.bio: A 35.5 m single-drop waterfall in the Otways 10 km inland from Lorne, with a lookout and about 240 steps to the base.

lorne-3.name: Sheoak Falls
lorne-3.bio: A 15.8 m waterfall on Sheoak Creek beside the Great Ocean Road in Great Otway National Park, about 6 km from Lorne.

lorne-4.name: Kennett River
lorne-4.bio: Great Ocean Road settlement between Lorne and Apollo Bay, where wild koalas live in the gums along Grey River Road.

apollo-bay-1.name: Cape Otway Lightstation
apollo-bay-1.bio: Victoria's oldest working lighthouse on Cape Otway, a heritage precinct with whale watching in winter and spring.

apollo-bay-2.name: Maits Rest
apollo-bay-2.bio: An 800 m self-guided circuit walk through cool temperate rainforest in Great Otway National Park near Apollo Bay.

apollo-bay-3.name: Hopetoun Falls
apollo-bay-3.bio: An 18 m single-drop waterfall on the Aire River in Great Otway National Park, reached by a 1 km return walk.

apollo-bay-4.name: Triplet Falls
apollo-bay-4.bio: A 1.8 km walk through ancient rainforest to a platform viewing three cascades, past an old timber mill site.

apollo-bay-5.name: Beauchamp Falls
apollo-bay-5.bio: An 18.7 m single-drop waterfall near Beech Forest in the Otways, reached by a walk of about 3 km return.

apollo-bay-6.name: Otway Fly
apollo-bay-6.bio: A 600 m steel Treetop Walk 25 to 30 m above the Otway forest floor, with a 47 m Spiral Tower and guided ziplines.

apollo-bay-7.name: Johanna Beach
apollo-bay-7.bio: Unpatrolled 3.6 km surf beach in Great Otway National Park that hosted the 1970 World Surfing Championships.

apollo-bay-8.name: Blanket Bay
apollo-bay-8.bio: Sheltered beach on Cape Otway's east side, calmed by a reef, with a drive-in campground and Great Ocean Walk links.

port-campbell-national-park-1.name: Twelve Apostles
port-campbell-national-park-1.bio: Limestone stacks up to 50 m high off the Great Ocean Road, six visible from the main viewpoint, glowing at sunset.

port-campbell-national-park-2.name: Loch Ard Gorge
port-campbell-national-park-2.bio: Limestone gorge with a sheltered beach, where two of the 54 people aboard the 1878 Loch Ard wreck survived.

port-campbell-national-park-3.name: Gibson Steps
port-campbell-national-park-3.bio: A staircase of 86 steps cut into the cliffs leads down to Gibson Beach, with the Gog and Magog stacks just offshore.

port-campbell-national-park-4.name: London Arch
port-campbell-national-park-4.bio: Offshore arch near Port Campbell whose shore-side span collapsed in 1990, stranding two tourists on the remaining one.

port-campbell-national-park-5.name: The Arch
port-campbell-national-park-5.bio: Weathered limestone sea arch, part blowhole, 6 km west of Port Campbell, reached by a short easy walk to lookouts.

port-campbell-national-park-6.name: The Grotto
port-campbell-national-park-6.bio: Natural rock window framing the coastline on the Shipwreck Coast, just beyond Port Campbell near London Bridge.

port-campbell-national-park-7.name: Bay of Islands
port-campbell-national-park-7.bio: Sea cliffs and rock stacks near Peterborough, quieter than the big stops, with whales offshore May to October.

port-campbell-national-park-8.name: Port Campbell
port-campbell-national-park-8.bio: Great Ocean Road town west of the Twelve Apostles, base for the Shipwreck Coast sights and whale spotting in season.

warrnambool-1.name: Flagstaff Hill Maritime Museum
warrnambool-1.bio: Maritime museum and village on Flagstaff Hill in Warrnambool, alongside the original lighthouses and garrison.

warrnambool-2.name: Logans Beach Whale Watching Platform
warrnambool-2.bio: Free viewing platform above Logans Beach, Warrnambool, where southern right whales calve, usually June to September.

warrnambool-3.name: Deep Blue Hot Springs
warrnambool-3.bio: Geothermal bathing sanctuary in Warrnambool with an indoor bath house, outdoor pools and two-hour sessions.

warrnambool-4.name: Tower Hill
warrnambool-4.bio: Wildlife reserve in a dormant volcano crater 15 km north-west of Warrnambool, with emus, koalas and walking trails.

warrnambool-5.name: Moyjil - Point Ritchie
warrnambool-5.bio: Headland at the Hopkins River mouth, Warrnambool, with lookouts over the reef and deep significance to the Peek Whurrung.

warrnambool-6.name: Hopkins Falls
warrnambool-6.bio: Victoria's widest cascades, 90 m across the Hopkins River 15 km from Warrnambool, fullest in winter or after rain.

warrnambool-7.name: Lake Pertobe
warrnambool-7.bio: Eight-hectare lakeside park on Warrnambool's foreshore with a giant-slide playground, trails and free barbecues.

portland-1.name: Cape Bridgewater
portland-1.bio: Cape 21 km south-west of Portland with high cliffs, a blowhole, a petrified forest and a fur seal colony lookout.

portland-2.name: Cape Nelson
portland-2.bio: A 32 m lighthouse lit in 1884 at the end of a scenic drive from Portland, with daily 11:30am tours that climb it.

portland-3.name: Discovery Bay Coastal Park
portland-3.bio: A 50 km coastal park west of Cape Nelson to the South Australian border, with cliffs, long beaches and mobile dunes.

portland-4.name: Great South West Walk
portland-4.bio: A 262 km loop trail from Portland through coast, forest and Discovery Bay, walkable in day or overnight sections.

port-fairy.name: Port Fairy
port-fairy.bio: Fishing and tourist town on the Moyne River, with a causeway to Griffiths Island's lighthouse and shearwater colony.

griffiths-island-lighthouse.name: Griffiths Island Lighthouse
griffiths-island-lighthouse.bio: Bluestone lighthouse from about 1859 on Griffiths Island, reached by causeway; the grounds are open but the tower is not.

the-crags.name: The Crags
the-crags.bio: Wind-sculpted coastal rock formations 12 km west of Port Fairy, with lookouts over the Southern Ocean.

budj-bim-cultural-landscape.name: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape
budj-bim-cultural-landscape.bio: World Heritage landscape of Gunditjmara eel-farming channels and weirs, with guided tours from Lake Condah.

mount-eccles-national-park.name: Budj Bim National Park
mount-eccles-national-park.bio: Volcanic national park with a crater lake, lava canals and caves, and four walks including the crater rim.

mount-leura.name: Mount Leura
mount-leura.bio: Extinct volcano near Camperdown with a 100 m deep crater, and a summit lookout reached by road toward the Grampians.
